name: SCENTAI Catalog Selection Policy
purpose: Select high-demand, high-quality, commercially useful fragrances without relying on a single retailer or community.
principles: Do not rank products by affiliate commission.
Do not treat a high community rating with a tiny vote count as equivalent to a proven bestseller.
Use multiple independent demand signals when available.
Keep women's and feminine-leaning unisex coverage as an explicit portfolio objective.
Prefer products that improve recommendation coverage, price comparison, or original-vs-alternative clusters.
Never invent sales counts when retailers only expose bestseller ordering or labels.
First-party SCENTAI demand may reprioritize research but never bypass evidence, QA, or live-promotion gates.

retailer_demand.description: Bestseller/ranking evidence from German fragrance retailers. Exact unit sales are used only when a source publishes them.
retailer_demand.method: Normalize rank/placement per retailer; combine multiple retailers; do not fabricate sales volumes.

community_strength.description: Combine rating quality and confidence from the number of community ratings/reviews.
community_strength.method: Use a Bayesian/confidence-adjusted rating so 9.0 from 50 votes cannot outrank 8.4 from thousands solely on raw score.

cross_merchant_coverage.description: Reward products available from multiple approved merchants because they enable genuine price comparison.
cross_merchant_coverage.method: Count verified merchant offers/feeds; cap the contribution so availability never dominates recommendation quality.

trend_momentum.description: Current awards, recent bestseller movement, new-release attention, and repeated SCENTAI search demand.

first_party_demand.purpose: Use privacy-minimized SCENTAI catalog search demand as one verified input to the existing trend_momentum component.

unique_session_proxy.note: Aggregated search rows cannot safely deduplicate the same anonymous session across multiple terms, so candidate aggregation uses the strongest matched term's unique-session count as a conservative proxy.

first_party_demand.integration_rule: Demand can raise trend_momentum only up to the existing 10-point cap. It never adds points outside the 0-100 policy weights.
first_party_demand.privacy_rule: Only privacy-minimized catalog search analytics may be used. Do not use prompts, IP addresses, emails, customer names, or raw personal data.
guardrails: One user's repeated search activity must not be treated as broad market demand.
First-party demand does not replace retailer or community evidence.
A no-result search can raise research priority but cannot create or verify a product identity.
Demand ranking never includes affiliate commission.

portfolio_fit.description: Fill gaps in audience, season, occasion, price tier, scent family, and original/alternative clusters.
guardrails: Women's and feminine-leaning unisex coverage must increase materially from the current baseline.
Do not let the catalog become only designer bestsellers or only dupes.
Maintain fresh, gourmand, floral, woody, amber/oriental, musky and aquatic coverage.

minimum_evidence_before_live.identity: Exact brand, fragrance name and concentration verified.
minimum_evidence_before_live.demand: At least two independent demand/community signals, or one very strong retailer signal plus verified catalog-gap rationale.
minimum_evidence_before_live.community: If community rating is used, record rating and vote/review count together.
minimum_evidence_before_live.commerce: Merchant availability may be absent at candidate stage but must never be invented.
minimum_evidence_before_live.relationships: Clone/inspired/alternative labels require separate evidence review.

audience_policy.note: Feminine/masculine leaning is an editorial scent-style descriptor, not a restriction on who can wear a fragrance.

working_catalog_mix.review_rule: Revisit this mix once SCENTAI has enough real search, clickout and conversion data. Do not assume one gender buys more fragrance without current Germany-specific evidence.

audience_policy.counting_rule: Feminine-leaning unisex remains in the unisex bucket, not the women-only bucket.
audience_policy.batch_rule: Individual batches may deviate when needed to correct catalog gaps, but the rolling live-catalog mix should stay near the working target.

promotion_rules.score_65_79: Good candidate; promote when it fills a catalog gap or has strong merchant coverage.
promotion_rules.score_50_64: Keep in backlog; needs stronger evidence or clearer portfolio role.

emerging_release_fast_track.purpose: Catch genuinely hot new releases before stable retailer sales histories exist.
eligibility: Release is new enough that normal annual sales history is not yet available.
At least two independent demand/community signals are positive.
Early community sample is large enough to be meaningful for the age of the release.
The product fills a real catalog or trend-discovery role.

current_thresholds.preferred_community_quality: Clearly above the source's ordinary average for a new release

guardrails: Fast-track means candidate priority, not automatic live publication.
Exact product identity, concentration and size still require verification.
Early hype must be rechecked after the initial launch window.
Do not compare raw scores across communities without accounting for scale and vote count.

research_priority.purpose: Order the not-yet-staged candidate research queue without changing live-promotion eligibility.
rules: Exclude candidates already present in the verified staging catalog.
If verified selection_score_components exist, use the demand-adjusted 0-100 selection score, with demand constrained to trend_momentum.
If no numeric selection score exists, keep the demand score separate rather than fabricating missing external evidence.
Use demand only as a deterministic queue/tie-break signal when external selection evidence is otherwise equal.
Surface high-demand search terms that match no existing candidate as new research opportunities.
Research priority is not publication approval.
